cases.sentence: Вдруг ему показался за дверью какой-то ___.
cases.explain: «странный звук» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “ ‘Grant leave to retire to his country seat to an old man who is already in any case dishonored by being unable to fulfill the great and glorious task for which he was chosen. I shall await your most gracious permission here in hospital, that I may not have to play the part of a secretary rather than commander in the army. My removal from the army does not produce the slightest stir—a blind man has left it. There are thousands such as I in Russia.’

cases.sentence: В ту минуту, как он входил, он увидел, что нянька с ___ спрятала что-то от него, и что княжны Марьи уже не было у кроватки.
cases.explain: «испуганным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “The field marshal is angry with the Emperor and he punishes us all, isn’t it logical?

cases.sentence: Как это часто бывает после ___ и долгого волнения, на него нашел беспричинный страх: ему пришло в голову, что ребенок умер.
cases.explain: «долгой бессонницы» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Just as he went in he saw that the nurse was hiding something from him with a scared look and that Princess Márya was no longer by the cot.

cases.sentence: «Всё кончено», подумал он, и ___ выступил у него на лбу.
cases.explain: «холодный пот» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “My dear,” he heard what seemed to him her despairing whisper behind him. As often happens after long sleeplessness and long anxiety, he was seized by an unreasoning panic—it occurred to him that the child was dead. All that he saw and heard seemed to confirm this terror.

cases.sentence: Наконец он увидал его: ___, раскидавшись, лежал поперег кроватки, спустив голову ниже подушки и во сне чмокал, перебирая губками, и ровно дышал.
cases.explain: «румяный мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “My dear,” he heard what seemed to him her despairing whisper behind him. As often happens after long sleeplessness and long anxiety, he was seized by an unreasoning panic—it occurred to him that the child was dead. All that he saw and heard seemed to confirm this terror.

cases.sentence: Лучистые глаза княжны Марьи, в матовом полусвете полога, блестели более обыкновенного от ___, которые стояли в них.
cases.explain: «счастливых слёз» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy looked at his sister. In the dim shadow of the curtain her luminous eyes shone more brightly than usual from the tears of joy that were in them. She leaned over to her brother and kissed him, slightly catching the curtain of the cot. Each made the other a warning gesture and stood still in the dim light beneath the curtain as if not wishing to leave that seclusion where they three were shut off from all the world. Prince Andréy was the first to move away, ruffling his hair against the muslin of the curtain. “Yes, this is the one thing left me now,” he said with a sigh.

cases.sentence: Они погрозили друг другу, еще постояли в ___ полога, как бы не желая расстаться с этим миром, в котором они втроем были отделены от всего света.
cases.explain: «матовом свете» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
